validity.researcher_notes: gem.wiki returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) to WebFetch, consistent with the scope note that the citation harvest failed for this whole batch — wiki_citations.json is empty for P4178 as expected, not evidence of an unsourced row per se. However, exhaustive open-web checks (Bing, Google, DuckDuckGo lite/html, Wikipedia full-text search, Marginalia — note: this session's WebSearch tool budget was exhausted, so all checks below used WebFetch against search engines directly) for '"Manjiwala" "Pezu" gas pipeline', '"Kala Manjiwala"', 'Pezu Tank gas pipeline SNGPL', and 'Krapa-Manjiwala' turned up NOTHING except GEM's own wiki pages for P4178 and its sister row P4177 (Krapa-Manjiwala Gas Pipeline) — i.e. every hit traces back to GEM, none independent. 'Kala Manjiwala' as a place name produces zero gazetteer/news hits anywhere outside GEM. Wikipedia's own article on Pezu (Darra Pezu, Lakki Marwat) makes no mention of any gas pipeline, SNGPL, or Kala Manjiwala. SNGPL's own site (sngpl.com.pk) has no accessible network-map detail (nav-only, JS-gated); its homepage verifies live (200, contains 'Sui Northern') but only as generic confirmation SNGPL exists/operates in the region — it does not name this pipeline, so it is not cited below. The single piece of genuine independent evidence found is INSIDE this project's own already-ingested GulfPub (Petroleum Economist) dataset: recon_gulfpub_crosswalk.json already matches an SNGPL-operated, 8-inch record 'Pezu - Tank' (ref_id gulfpub:gas:9718, 34.5 km, operator 'Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Ltd') against P4178 at only 'yellow' confidence (composite 0.5867) with a flagged 35% length delta (34.5 km vs GEM's 53.29 km) and a route IoU of just 0.016 — crucially, that record's endpoints are Pezu→Tank, NOT Kala Manjiwala→Pezu. Tank and Kala Manjiwala are not the same place (Tank is a separate district south of Lakki Marwat toward D.I. Khan; Kala Manjiwala, per P4177, sits toward Karak/Krapa, roughly the opposite direction from Pezu). So this GulfPub record independently corroborates only that SNGPL operates SOME 8-inch transmission-scale line running through Pezu — it does NOT corroborate the specific Kala Manjiwala→Pezu routing or the 53.29 km length recorded for P4178; it may instead describe a different, GEM-missing continuation south/east of Pezu. The OSM recon run (match_diff.json) has zero trace for P4178 at all (bucketed gem_only, 'no reference match'), which is unsurprising for rural OSM coverage in KP but adds no corroboration either way. This row also carries the LastUpdated=2023-07-07 bulk-load stamp shared by dozens of other short KP/Punjab feeder segments in this scope, several of which likely originated from a single digitized SNGPL network table — plausible in kind, but this specific segment's naming and exact spec are not independently locatable anywhere I could reach. Classification (transmission, gas) and district assignment (Pezu in Lakki Marwat) are internally consistent and not disputed; ownership (SNGPL, 100%) is directionally plausible (SNGPL is the confirmed KP transmission utility and is independently named as operator of the nearby Pezu-Tank line) but not confirmed for this exact PID by any source that names it. No duplicate found against the 63-row roster: P4177 (Krapa→Kala Manjiwala) and P4178 (Kala Manjiwala→Pezu) are sequential, non-overlapping legs of one corridor, not the same physical pipe recorded twice.

summary: P4178 (Manjiwala-Pezu Gas Pipeline): existence concern — every open-web trace of this named pipeline and its 'Kala Manjiwala' endpoint resolves only to GEM's own wiki pages; the lone independent lead (GulfPub's SNGPL 'Pezu-Tank' 8-inch record) has different endpoints and a 35% length delta, so it corroborates general SNGPL infrastructure at Pezu but not this specific segment. No refs met the verification bar; all seven ref units (Status/Fuel/PipelineType/Length/Diameter/Location/Owner) remain UNRESOLVED, flagged for human escalation rather than left silently unsourced.
